claim: ans: "Protected terms (Château, Clos, Cru, Vintage/Port, Classic…)"; exp: "Why an Aussie 'Port' became Tawny and 'Sherry' became Apera at home too."
because: Port (Porto) and Sherry (Jerez-Xérès-Sherry) are protected geographical indications, not traditional terms. Australia dropped them under the GI provisions of the 2008 EU–Australia Agreement on Trade in Wine, which came into force in 2010. The same agreement expressly lets Australia keep the traditional expressions tawny, ruby, cream and vintage. So the name change came from GI protection, and 'Vintage' is a term non-EU wines can use under agreements, as the 2006 US–EU agreement also allows Château, Clos and Vintage for US wines.
fix: ans: "Protected traditional terms (Château, Clos, Cru, Classic…) in the EU market unless a bilateral agreement authorises them"; exp: "Distinct from GI protection: Port and Sherry are protected geographical indications, which is why Australian 'Port' became Tawny and 'Sherry' became Apera under the 2008 EU–Australia wine agreement."
